summary: I wrote a read-only concept memo comparing OUTRAM PARK with NUS-H2: SP/design/outram_concepts.md (C:/Users/Alf/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Ray-Claude-Ray-Debug-VS-Code/b29325b8-d1b9-49cd-bfe6-262261d7ffef/scratchpad/design/outram_concepts.md). It has 36 numbered items. Each gives the engine/ module it bears on, the concept in my own words, the primary source where OUTRAM names one, the OUTRAM file:line (citation only, main 9af23fdb1), what NUS-H2 has now (from reading, nothing run), and an acceptance test with a tolerance or pass rule. A section-0 table records the maturity and human sign-off each OUTRAM crate claims for itself, without overstating it. The memo contains no OUTRAM code, no transcribed pseudocode and no identifiers beyond citation paths. On the user's question: citing concepts and primary-source equations is fine. Copying a function's control flow step by step is avoided because it can carry the code's expression, so the memo uses tests and equations instead. The main new finding (my own calculation, not an engine run): the absorber's SRK fugacity coefficient treats every non-CO2 mole as water vapour. At 26.8 bar that gives a liquid-like root and phi_CO2 of about 80 to 560, so plant-absorber p* may be divided by that factor. I changed nothing in REPO, built or ran nothing in OUTRAM, and made no commits.
